To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a p53-dependent transcriptional repressor can be exploited to selectively kill p53-deficient tumor cells by inhibiting the expression of a prodrug-activating enzyme, and that the system can be used in a uniform genetic system to demonstrate p53-dependent killing of tumor cells.
we have developed an approach for selective killing of tumor cells that uses the status of the tumor suppressor protein p53.

we have shown that a designed repressor, K25-5F, can be used to selectively repress the expression of a gene, HSV-TK, and thus selectively protect normal cells from the effects of the antiviral drug, ganciclovivir.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of novel gene regulatory elements that may be suitable for use in cancer gene therapy.
the design of synthetic repressors that can be used in combination with p53 status to achieve selective killing of tumor cells.
the design and use of transcriptional repressors for the regulation of gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system described here provides a novel approach to cancer therapy, which may be suitable for future development.
the use of a p53-dependent repressor to selectively reduce the expression of HSVTK and subsequent GCV-mediated cell death may be an approach to selective tumor cell killing.
we have demonstrated that the K2- 5F system is a useful approach for selective cell killing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a system to preferentially kill p53-deficient tumor cells using a designed transcriptional regulator, K2- 5F, and a prodrug.

we have established a system for selective killing of p53-deficient tumor cells by exploiting p53 status to induce a repressor, K-5F, which selectively reduces the expression a prodrug activation gene.
we have developed an approach for selective killing of p53-deficient cancer cells.

we developed a system for selective killing of cancer cells that are p53-negative.
